mechanism: Exact shifted-fiber Hellinger affinity optimizes public unitaries that nondestructively imprint one fixed secret character on the unaltered native source.
underfull_conclusion: At D=G/9, population minimum squared generator error exceeds16/9 even with unbounded gate cost.
overfull_escape: Existence obstruction weakens with extra copies; normalized fiber transport is still not compiled efficiently.
not_covered: General collective POVMs, source-changing instruments or postselected factories.
Label-adaptive offsets without a separate probability argument.
Classically learned small-R moment models that do not require a nondemolition action on original states.
A generic quantum lower bound, IID-average hardness or a new quantum speedup.
proof_obligations: Independent review of orthogonal-fiber unitary optimum and fixed-offset IID population law.
For any positive native spectral proposal, implement controlled generators and charge state/copy/error costs.
For an enlarged-batch fiber construction, supply a clean normalized fiber transform, not just a dense optimum.
Do not replace operator period with the weaker equality U^q=I when claiming full-root coverage.
Compare against direct classical inference and known native/DCP sieves in the same source regime.
falsifiers: Optimal unitary reference exceeds or fails to attain the exact radical optimum.
Complete native ensemble disagrees with the ordered-pair or chi-squared identities.
A diagonal/commutant projector readout is promoted as secret-informative.
A label-chosen direction inherits a fixed-direction population bound.
A dense basis extension is claimed to be an efficient coherent fiber compiler.
